lanes.label: On the way to the cross
Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: The gospel of Mark, from “the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God” (1:1) through Jesus’ ministry in Galilee, the road to Jerusalem and his death, to the empty tomb and commission.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Mark is about and where it begins and ends?
ev: Describe the movement of the book: John and the start of ministry (1), Galilee (1-8), the way to Jerusalem (8-10), the last week and passion (11-15), the empty tomb (16)
Say what Mark calls the book in 1:1

nodes.d: Mark opens with the beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God; John baptizes in the wilderness for repentance and says one mightier will baptize with the Holy Ghost.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who John was and what he said about the one coming after him?
ev: Say how Mark begins his book
Describe John’s message and appearance

nodes.t: The baptism and temptation of Jesus
nodes.d: Jesus is baptized by John, the Spirit descends like a dove and a voice calls him beloved Son; the Spirit then drives him into the wilderness, where he is tempted forty days by Satan.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened at Jesus’ baptism and in the wilderness?
ev: Describe what happened at the Jordan
Say where Jesus went next and for how long

nodes.t: Jesus preaches the kingdom and calls four fishermen
nodes.d: After John is imprisoned Jesus preaches in Galilee that the time is fulfilled and the kingdom of God is at hand, and calls Simon, Andrew, James and John from their nets.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jesus called his first disciples?
ev: Say what Jesus preached
Name the four fishermen

nodes.t: The man with an unclean spirit in the synagogue
nodes.d: At Capernaum Jesus teaches with authority and commands an unclean spirit, which cries that he is the Holy One of God, to come out, and the people are amazed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus did in the Capernaum synagogue?
ev: Retell what the unclean spirit said
Say how the people responded

nodes.t: Healing Peter’s mother-in-law and the crowds
nodes.d: Jesus heals Simon’s wife’s mother, then at evening heals many and casts out devils; before dawn he prays alone in a solitary place and says he must preach in other towns.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus did that evening and next morning?
ev: Retell the evening at the door
Say why Jesus left Capernaum

nodes.d: A leper kneels and asks to be made clean; Jesus, moved with compassion, touches him and heals him, telling him to show himself to the priest, but the man spreads the news.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the leper asked and what Jesus did?
ev: Retell the healing
Say what happened after the man disobeyed

nodes.t: The paralytic let down through the roof
nodes.d: Four men break through a roof to lower a paralysed man to Jesus, who forgives his sins; when scribes call it blasphemy he heals the man to show that the Son of man has power on earth to forgive sins.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus did for the man lowered through the roof?
ev: Retell how the man reached Jesus
Say why the scribes objected

nodes.t: Levi called and the question about fasting
nodes.d: Jesus calls Levi the tax collector and eats with publicans and sinners, saying he came to call sinners; asked about fasting, he speaks of the bridegroom, new cloth and new wine.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus ate with sinners and what he said about fasting?
ev: Say whom Jesus called and what Pharisees objected to
Explain the bridegroom saying

nodes.t: Lord of the sabbath: the grainfield
nodes.d: When disciples pluck grain on the sabbath, Jesus cites David eating the shewbread and says the sabbath was made for man and the Son of man is Lord of it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said about the sabbath?
ev: State the objection and Jesus’ example
Explain “the sabbath was made for man”

nodes.d: In the synagogue Jesus asks whether it is lawful to do good or evil on the sabbath, heals a man’s withered hand, and the Pharisees and Herodians plot to destroy him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the Pharisees plotted against Jesus after this healing?
ev: Retell the healing and Jesus’ question
Say what the Pharisees did

nodes.t: The multitudes and the appointing of the twelve
nodes.d: Crowds from many regions come to Jesus; he goes up a mountain and appoints twelve to be with him, to preach and to have power to heal and cast out devils, and Mark names them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus appointed the twelve for?
ev: Name several of the twelve
Say what the twelve were appointed to do

nodes.t: The Beelzebub charge and Jesus’ family
nodes.d: Scribes from Jerusalem say Jesus casts out devils by the prince of devils; he answers that a divided kingdom cannot stand, warns of blaspheming the Holy Ghost, and says whoever does God’s will is his brother, sister and mother.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the scribes said and how Jesus answered?
ev: Summarise Jesus’ reply about a divided house
Say who Jesus calls his family

nodes.d: Teaching from a boat, Jesus tells the parable of the sower and explains it privately to his disciples: the word sown on the path, stony ground, thorns and good ground.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the four soils stand for?
ev: Retell the four soils
Give Jesus’ explanation of each

nodes.t: The lamp, the growing seed and the mustard seed
nodes.d: Jesus says what is hidden will be made known, speaks of the measure you give, tells of seed growing by itself until harvest and of the mustard seed, and explains all things privately to his disciples.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Jesus says the kingdom of God is like in 4:26-32?
ev: Explain the lamp saying
Compare the growing seed and the mustard seed

nodes.d: Crossing the sea in the evening, the disciples are swamped by a storm while Jesus sleeps; he rebukes the wind and says to the sea “Peace, be still”, and they ask what manner of man this is.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus did in the storm?
ev: Retell the storm
State the disciples’ question in 4:41

nodes.d: Jesus meets a man living among tombs with an unclean spirit; the many spirits (Legion) are sent into two thousand swine, and the healed man is told to tell his friends what the Lord has done and proclaims it in Decapolis.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the man called Legion?
ev: Describe the man’s condition
Say what Jesus told him to do after healing

nodes.t: Jairus’ daughter and the woman who touched his garment
nodes.d: Jairus begs Jesus to heal his dying daughter; on the way a woman bleeding for twelve years touches his garment and is healed; Jesus then raises the girl, telling Jairus not to fear but to believe.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus did for the woman and for Jairus’ daughter?
ev: Retell both healings
Say what Jesus said to Jairus when news came the girl was dead

nodes.d: Jesus teaches in his home synagogue; people are offended that he is the carpenter, Mary’s son, and he can do few mighty works there, marvelling at their unbelief.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened when Jesus taught at Nazareth?
ev: Say why they took offence
Quote or paraphrase the saying about a prophet’s honour

nodes.t: The twelve sent out two by two
nodes.d: Jesus sends the twelve out in pairs with power over unclean spirits and instructions to take little; they preach repentance, cast out devils and anoint many sick with oil.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jesus sent out the twelve?
ev: List the instructions about what to take
Say what the twelve did

nodes.t: Herod and the death of John the Baptist
nodes.d: Hearing of Jesus, Herod fears John has risen; Mark recounts John’s imprisonment for rebuking Herod over Herodias, and how Herod’s oath at his birthday supper led to John’s beheading.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how John the Baptist died?
ev: Retell why John was imprisoned
Describe the oath and its result

nodes.d: The apostles return and Jesus takes them apart, but crowds follow; Jesus teaches them, then feeds about five thousand with five loaves and two fishes, with twelve baskets of fragments.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the feeding of the five thousand?
ev: Say what Jesus did with the loaves and fishes
Give the numbers fed and left over

nodes.d: Jesus sends the disciples by ship while he prays on the mountain; in the fourth watch he comes to them walking on the sea, tells them not to be afraid, and the wind ceases; Mark says their hearts were hardened about the loaves.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of Jesus walking on the sea?
ev: Retell what Jesus did and said
Say what Mark says the disciples had not understood

nodes.t: Tradition of the elders and what defiles
nodes.d: Pharisees fault the disciples for eating with unwashed hands; Jesus quotes Isaiah on lip service, charges them with setting aside God’s commandment through Corban, and says what comes out of the heart defiles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus says defiles a person?
ev: Explain Jesus’ Corban example
List what proceeds from the heart (7:21-22)

nodes.d: In the region of Tyre a Greek woman begs Jesus to cast a spirit out of her daughter; after his word about the children’s bread she replies about crumbs, and he tells her the devil has gone out.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the woman said and what Jesus did?
ev: Retell the conversation
Say how the daughter was healed

nodes.d: In Decapolis people bring a deaf man with a speech impediment; Jesus takes him aside, touches his ears and tongue, says “Ephphatha”, and he hears and speaks.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the healing of the deaf man?
ev: Describe what Jesus did and said
Say what the crowd said (7:37)

nodes.d: Jesus has compassion on a crowd three days without food and feeds about four thousand with seven loaves and a few fishes, leaving seven baskets.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the feeding of the four thousand?
ev: Give the numbers of loaves and baskets
Compare with the five thousand

nodes.t: Seeking a sign and the leaven of the Pharisees and Herod
nodes.d: Pharisees seek a sign from heaven and Jesus refuses; in the boat he warns against the leaven of the Pharisees and Herod and reminds the disciples of the loaves and baskets in the two feedings.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus asked the disciples to remember the baskets?
ev: Say what Jesus refused to give
Recall the numbers Jesus asked the disciples about

nodes.d: At Bethsaida Jesus leads a blind man outside the town, lays hands on him twice, and he sees clearly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jesus healed the blind man at Bethsaida?
ev: Describe the two stages of the healing
Say what Jesus told the man afterwards

nodes.t: Peter’s confession and the first prediction of the cross
nodes.d: At Caesarea Philippi Peter says Jesus is the Christ; Jesus begins to teach that the Son of man must suffer, be killed and rise after three days, rebukes Peter, and calls followers to deny themselves and take up the cross.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who Peter said Jesus is and what Jesus said must happen?
ev: State what the people and Peter said of Jesus
Explain the call to take up the cross

nodes.d: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James and John on a high mountain with Elias and Moses; a voice from the cloud calls him beloved Son and says hear him; he tells them not to speak of it until he rises.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the transfiguration?
ev: Describe what the disciples saw and heard
Say what Jesus said about Elias

nodes.t: The boy with a dumb spirit
nodes.d: A father brings his son tormented by a spirit; Jesus says all things are possible to him that believes, the father cries “Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief”, and Jesus casts the spirit out, saying this kind comes out by prayer.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the father said and how Jesus helped the boy?
ev: Retell the father’s plea and Jesus’ answer
Say what Jesus told the disciples about prayer

nodes.t: Second prediction, who is greatest and stumbling blocks
nodes.d: Jesus again foretells his death and rising; the disciples argue who is greatest, and he sets a child among them, says whoever is not against them is for them, warns against offending little ones and speaks of the fire that is not quenched and having salt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said about greatness and little ones?
ev: Say what Jesus taught about being first
Explain the warning about offences

nodes.t: Marriage and divorce, and blessing the children
nodes.d: Tested about divorce, Jesus points to creation: male and female, leaving father and mother and becoming one flesh; later he welcomes children, saying the kingdom of God belongs to such and must be received as a child.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus taught about marriage and about children?
ev: Say what Jesus cites from creation about marriage
Explain what he says about the children

nodes.t: The rich man who went away sorrowful
nodes.d: A man runs to ask what he must do to inherit eternal life; Jesus loves him and tells him to sell all and follow, and he leaves sad; Jesus teaches about the difficulty of riches and what God can do and promises to those who leave all.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus asked of the rich man and why he left sad?
ev: Say what Jesus lists and then asks of the man
Explain “with God all things are possible”

nodes.t: Third prediction, James and John, and the ransom
nodes.d: On the way to Jerusalem Jesus foretells his betrayal, mocking and rising; James and John ask for seats at his right and left, and Jesus says whoever would be great must serve, for the Son of man came to give his life a ransom for many.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said about serving and about his life as a ransom?
ev: Describe what Jesus foretold
Explain 10:45

nodes.d: Leaving Jericho, blind Bartimaeus cries out to Jesus as son of David; told to be silent he cries more, Jesus calls him, asks what he wants, and he receives his sight and follows Jesus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Bartimaeus was healed?
ev: Retell what Bartimaeus said and did
Say what Jesus told him

nodes.d: Jesus sends two disciples for a colt that no one has ridden; he rides it as people spread garments and branches and shout Hosanna, blessing him that comes in the name of the Lord and the kingdom of David.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jesus entered Jerusalem?
ev: Retell how the colt was found
Say what the people shouted

nodes.t: The fig tree and the cleansing of the temple
nodes.d: Jesus curses a leafy fig tree without fruit, drives out sellers and moneychangers saying the house is for prayer for all nations, and next day the disciples see the fig tree withered; he teaches faith and forgiving when praying.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus did in the temple and what he taught about prayer?
ev: Retell the order of events
Say what Jesus taught about prayer

nodes.d: Chief priests, scribes and elders ask by what authority Jesus acts; he asks them whether John’s baptism was from heaven or of men, and when they will not answer he declines to answer them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jesus answered the authority question?
ev: State the question and counter-question
Explain why they would not answer

nodes.t: The parable of the vineyard tenants
nodes.d: A man plants a vineyard and lets it to husbandmen who beat and kill his servants and then his beloved son; Jesus cites the rejected stone that became head of the corner, and the rulers know the parable is against them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who the servants, son and husbandmen stand for?
ev: Retell the parable
Say what the rulers understood

nodes.d: Pharisees and Herodians ask if tribute to Caesar is lawful; Jesus asks for a penny, asks whose image it bears, and says to render to Caesar what is Caesar’s and to God what is God’s.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said about the coin?
ev: Say why they asked
Explain Jesus’ answer

nodes.d: Sadducees who deny the resurrection ask about a woman married to seven brothers; Jesus says they err not knowing the scriptures or God’s power, that the risen are as angels, and that God is God of the living, citing the bush.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus’ answer about the resurrection?
ev: Say what the Sadducees asked
Explain Jesus’ use of the words from the bush

nodes.d: A scribe asks which commandment is first; Jesus answers the Lord is one and to love him with all heart, soul, mind and strength, and second to love your neighbour as yourself; the scribe agrees and Jesus says he is not far from the kingdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say the two great commandments?
ev: State the two commandments
Say what the scribe added and what Jesus replied

nodes.t: David’s Lord and warning against the scribes
nodes.d: Teaching in the temple, Jesus asks how the Christ can be David’s son when David calls him Lord, and warns the people against scribes who love honour and devour widows’ houses.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus asked about David and the Christ?
ev: State the puzzle Jesus raised about David
List what he warns about the scribes

nodes.d: Sitting by the treasury, Jesus sees rich people give much and a poor widow give two mites, and says she has given more than all because she gave all her living.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus praised the widow?
ev: Describe what the widow gave
Explain why Jesus said she gave more

nodes.t: The Olivet discourse: signs and the abomination
nodes.d: Leaving the temple, Jesus foretells the buildings’ destruction and on the Mount of Olives warns of deceivers, wars, persecution and the gospel preached to all nations; he warns of the abomination of desolation, great affliction and false Christs.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what Jesus said to watch for?
ev: State the disciples’ question (13:4)
List the warnings Jesus gave

nodes.t: The coming of the Son of man and the call to watch
nodes.d: After the tribulation the Son of man will be seen coming in clouds and gather the elect; Jesus gives the fig tree parable, says no one but the Father knows the day, and tells everyone to watch.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus told his disciples to watch?
ev: Describe the coming of the Son of man
Say what Jesus commands in 13:37

nodes.t: The plot, the anointing at Bethany and Judas’ offer
nodes.d: Two days before Passover the priests seek to take Jesus; a woman pours spikenard on his head at Simon the leper’s house and Jesus says she anointed his body for burial; Judas goes to the chief priests.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the woman did and what Jesus said about it?
ev: Retell the anointing and the objection
Say what Judas offered

nodes.t: The Passover meal and the Lord’s Supper
nodes.d: Disciples prepare the Passover in an upper room; Jesus says one of the twelve will betray him, gives them bread as his body and the cup as his blood of the new testament shed for many, and says he will drink new in the kingdom of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus did with the bread and cup at the Passover?
ev: Describe what Jesus said over the bread and cup
Say what he said about the new testament

nodes.d: Jesus foretells that the sheep will be scattered and Peter will deny him; in Gethsemane he prays “Abba, Father” that the cup might pass yet not his will, and finds the disciples asleep.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus prayed in Gethsemane?
ev: Retell Jesus’ prayer
Say what Peter said and what Jesus answered

nodes.d: Judas comes with a crowd and betrays Jesus with a kiss; one drawn sword cuts off a servant’s ear; Jesus says the scriptures must be fulfilled, all the disciples flee, and a young man runs away leaving a linen cloth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jesus was arrested?
ev: Describe the betrayal
Say what the disciples did

nodes.d: False witnesses disagree; asked if he is the Christ the Son of the Blessed, Jesus says “I am” and speaks of the Son of man at the right hand of power; the high priest charges blasphemy and they condemn him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the high priest asked and the council decided?
ev: Say what Jesus answered the high priest
Describe how the council treated him

nodes.d: In the high priest’s courtyard Peter denies Jesus three times; the cock crows twice, he remembers Jesus’ word and weeps.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Peter denied Jesus?
ev: Retell the three denials
Say what Peter did when he remembered

nodes.d: The council delivers Jesus to Pilate, who asks if he is King of the Jews; the crowd, moved by the priests, asks for Barabbas and cries for Jesus to be crucified; Pilate scourges Jesus and delivers him to be crucified.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the trial before Pilate?
ev: Say who was released
Say why Pilate gave in

nodes.d: Soldiers dress Jesus in purple and a crown of thorns and mock him; Simon of Cyrene carries his cross; he is crucified at Golgotha between two thieves under the title King of the Jews while others mock.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jesus was crucified?
ev: Describe the mockery
List what is said of the crucifixion

nodes.d: Darkness covers the land; Jesus cries “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” and dies; the temple veil tears, and the centurion says truly this man was the Son of God; women watch from afar.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what happened when Jesus died?
ev: List the signs and the centurion’s words
Name the women who watched

nodes.d: Joseph of Arimathaea asks Pilate for the body, wraps it in fine linen, lays it in a rock tomb and rolls a stone to the door; Mary Magdalene and Mary see where he is laid.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jesus was buried?
ev: Say who buried Jesus and where
Say who saw where he was laid

nodes.d: Early on the first day the women find the stone rolled away and a young man in white tells them Jesus is risen, and that he goes before them into Galilee; they flee in fear and say nothing to anyone.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the women found at the tomb?
ev: Retell what the women found and were told
Say how they responded

nodes.d: The longer ending tells that Jesus appeared first to Mary Magdalene, then to two and then to the eleven, rebuking their unbelief; he sends them to preach the gospel to every creature and is received up to the right hand of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus told the eleven to do and what happened to him afterwards?
ev: List those to whom Jesus appeared
State the commission in 16:15-16

nodes.t: Made in the image of God
nodes.d: Man and woman are made in God's image and given dominion; the same truth grounds the sanctity of human life after the flood.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Genesis 1:26-27 teaches about people, and why this matters?
ev: Explain what it means to be made in God's image using Genesis 1:26-27
Connect Genesis 9:6 to the value of human life

nodes.d: God plants a garden, places the man in it with a command, and forms the woman as a helper fit for him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the garden and the one thing God told the man not to do?
ev: Retell the formation of the man and the woman
State God's command about the tree (2:16-17)

nodes.d: Exodus tells of Israel enslaved in Egypt (1:1-14) and delivered through the plagues, Passover and the sea (chapters 7-15), then of the covenant at Sinai (19-24) and the tabernacle (25-40), ending with the glory of the LORD filling it (40:34-38).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Exodus in order, from the bondage in Egypt to the glory filling the tabernacle?
ev: Name the main sections: bondage, deliverance, the journey to Sinai, the law and covenant, and the tabernacle
Say where Exodus begins (1:1) and ends (40:38)

nodes.d: While keeping Jethro's flock at Horeb, Moses sees a bush burning without being consumed. God calls him by name from it, declares the ground holy, identifies himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and says he has seen Israel's affliction and will send Moses to Pharaoh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened at the burning bush and what God said to Moses there?
ev: Describe what Moses saw and what God told him to do with his shoes (3:2-5)
Say what God said he had seen and heard (3:7-9)
Say what God sent Moses to do (3:10)

nodes.d: God speaks all these words, beginning by saying he is the LORD who brought Israel out of Egypt. They cover having no other gods, no images, not taking his name in vain, remembering the sabbath, honouring father and mother, and not killing, committing adultery, stealing, bearing false witness or coveting.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say the Ten Commandments in order and say what comes before them in 20:2?
ev: Recite the ten commandments in order from the Bible
Say what 20:2 says before the commandments begin
Say the reason given for the sabbath (20:11)

nodes.d: Laws deal with striking and killing, a refuge for accidental killing, striking or cursing parents, kidnapping, injuries, the life-for-life principle and an owner's responsibility for a goring ox or an open pit.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the difference between the cases in 21:12-14?
ev: Say how deliberate and accidental killing are treated differently (21:12-14)
Find the verses that state life for life, eye for eye (21:23-25)

nodes.t: "Ye shall be holy": laws for neighbours
nodes.d: Leviticus 19 gathers commands under the call to be holy because the LORD is holy: honouring parents, sabbaths, leaving gleanings for the poor, honest dealing, no partiality, loving one's neighbour as oneself, care for the stranger and just weights.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list some ways Leviticus 19 says holiness shows up in daily life?
ev: Name at least five commands from the chapter that deal with how to treat other people.
Find the command to love the neighbour (19:18) and the command about the stranger (19:33-34).

nodes.d: Deuteronomy records Moses' words to Israel on the plains of Moab in the fortieth year: a review of the journey, the ten commandments and the call to love the LORD, the laws for life in the land, the covenant renewal with its blessings and curses, Moses' song and blessing, and his death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain where Israel is and what Moses is doing throughout Deuteronomy?
ev: Describe Deuteronomy as Moses' speeches before Israel enters the land and name its main parts.

nodes.t: Hear, O Israel: love the LORD
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 6 gives the great command to love the LORD with all heart, soul and might because he is one LORD, to teach the words to children throughout the day, to remember him when blessed in the land, and to answer a child's question with the story of the exodus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means to love the LORD with all one's heart, soul and might?
ev: Say the command of 6:4-5 in your own words.
List the ways 6:6-9 says to keep the words before oneself and the children.

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 24:1-5 says a man who divorces his wife by a bill may not take her again after she has married another, and a newly married man is free from war for a year; 24:6-22 commands fair treatment of pledges, wages paid on the day, personal responsibility for sin, justice for stranger and orphan, and gleanings left for the poor.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Moses tells Israel to remember Egypt when treating the poor and stranger?
ev: Say what the law of 24:1-4 forbids.
Say how Israel was to treat a poor man's pledge and wages (24:10-15).
Find the reason repeated in 24:18, 22.

nodes.t: Punishment limits, the ox and the brother's widow
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 25:1-12 limits a beating to forty stripes, forbids muzzling an ox that treads out the corn, gives the duty of a brother to raise up a name for a dead brother and the shoe-loosing ceremony if he refuses, and a rule about a wife seizing a man in a fight.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the purpose of the law of the brother's widow in 25:5-10?
ev: Say the limit on flogging and the reason (25:3).
Describe the duty of a living brother to a dead brother's childless widow.

nodes.d: 1 Samuel runs from the birth of Samuel to Saul's death on Mount Gilboa: Samuel as prophet and judge, Israel's request for a king, Saul's reign and rejection, and David's rise and flight from Saul.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 1 Samuel from Hannah's prayer to the death of Saul?
ev: Name the three main figures: Samuel, Saul and David
Say how the book begins and ends (1:1-20, 31:1-13)

nodes.d: David gets the holy bread and Goliath's sword from Ahimelech the priest at Nob, where Doeg the Edomite sees him, then flees to Achish king of Gath and pretends to be mad.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what David did at Nob and at Gath?
ev: Say what David received at Nob (21:6, 21:9)
Say who saw David there (21:7)
Say how David escaped from Gath (21:13-15)

nodes.d: The Psalms are 150 songs and prayers addressed to or about the LORD: cries for help, confession, thanksgiving, praise of his creation and rule, songs about the king, and meditation on his law; the book closes with calls to praise (146-150).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name three kinds of psalm and read one verse from a psalm of each kind?
ev: Name several kinds of psalm (lament, thanksgiving, praise, royal, wisdom) and give one psalm number for each.

nodes.t: Psalm 22: my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
nodes.d: The speaker cries to God who seems far, is scorned and surrounded by enemies, his bones out of joint and garments divided, then declares God’s name in the congregation and says all the ends of the world shall remember and turn to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Psalm 22 moves from the opening cry to the closing praise?
ev: Read 22:1-21 and list the pictures of suffering.
Read 22:22-31 and say how the psalm ends.

nodes.t: Psalm 110: sit at my right hand; a priest after Melchizedek
nodes.d: The LORD says to the speaker’s Lord to sit at his right hand until his enemies are his footstool; he is a king sent to rule from Zion and a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek, sworn by the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Psalm 110:1 and 110:4 and say what the LORD says to the speaker’s Lord?
ev: Read 110:1-4 and say who speaks and to whom, and what is sworn.

nodes.t: Psalms 117-118: his mercy endureth for ever; the stone the builders refused
nodes.d: Psalm 117 calls all nations to praise the LORD for his great mercy and truth; Psalm 118 calls Israel to say his mercy endures for ever, tells of being delivered from distress, says it is better to trust the LORD than man, speaks of the stone the builders refused, and ends with giving thanks.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the refrain “his mercy endureth for ever” and the picture in Psalm 118:22-23?
ev: Read 118:5-9, 118:19-24 and 118:26-29 and list what is said about the LORD and the gate.

nodes.d: Isaiah son of Amoz sees visions concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah; the book moves from indictment and judgment to comfort, a servant, and new heavens and a new earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Isaiah was and describe, using Isaiah 1:1 and 40:1-2, how the book moves from rebuke to comfort?
ev: Name the four kings of Judah named in Isaiah 1:1
Describe the shift in tone between chapters 1-39 and chapter 40 using the texts

nodes.d: Isaiah sings of a beloved's well-tended vineyard that yields wild grapes, and the LORD explains that the vineyard is the house of Israel, for which he looked for justice and righteousness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the song of the vineyard and say what Isaiah 5:7 says it means?
ev: Retell what the owner did for the vineyard (5:1-2)
Say what he will do to it (5:5-6)
Explain who the vineyard is according to 5:7

nodes.t: Woe to Ariel: a sealed vision and a marvellous work
nodes.d: The LORD besieges Ariel, the city where David dwelt, then saves it from the nations; the people honour him with lips but not hearts, the vision is like a sealed book, and the deaf will hear and the blind see.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what 29:13 says about the people's worship?
ev: Describe the siege and sudden deliverance of Ariel (29:1-8)
Explain the charge in 29:13
Describe the change promised in 29:17-24

nodes.t: Comfort my people: the incomparable God
nodes.d: God tells his prophets to comfort Jerusalem because her iniquity is pardoned, a voice prepares the way of the LORD, the LORD comes as shepherd, and no one compares to him who gives strength to the weary.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD comforts Jerusalem in Isaiah 40:1-2 and who the LORD is compared to in 40:12-26?
ev: Quote the command and reason in Isaiah 40:1-2
Describe the voice crying in the wilderness (40:3-5)
Explain what 40:28-31 says about those who wait on the LORD

nodes.t: Foreigners and eunuchs welcomed; blind watchmen
nodes.d: The LORD says foreigners and eunuchs who hold to his covenant and keep sabbaths will be joyful in his house of prayer for all peoples, while blind watchmen and greedy shepherds are condemned.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who the LORD welcomes in Isaiah 56:3-8 and what his house is called?
ev: Say who is welcomed in Isaiah 56:3-7
Quote what the house is called (56:7)
Describe the charge against the watchmen (56:10-12)

nodes.d: Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, a priest of Anathoth, receives the word of the LORD from the thirteenth year of Josiah to the exile after Zedekiah's eleventh year, warning Judah of judgment from the north and promising restoration and a new covenant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Jeremiah was and during whose reigns the word of the LORD came to him according to Jeremiah 1:1-3?
ev: Name the kings during whose reigns the word came (Jeremiah 1:1-3)
Explain that the book is not arranged only in the order of the events it describes, using examples from its dates

nodes.d: At the gate of the LORD's house Jeremiah says not to trust "the temple of the LORD"; the LORD cites Shiloh, forbids Jeremiah to pray for the people, and condemns worship of the queen of heaven and child burning in Tophet.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jeremiah told the people not to trust in the temple of the LORD in Jeremiah 7:1-15?
ev: Explain what the people trusted and what the LORD required (7:3-7)
Say how the LORD compares the temple to Shiloh (7:12-14)
Describe the sins at Tophet (7:30-34)

nodes.d: Daniel and his friends are taken to Babylon, serve under Babylonian and Persian kings, and are delivered in the furnace and lions' den; Daniel interprets dreams and receives visions of kingdoms, the Ancient of days, and the end.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name Daniel and his three friends and say how the book of Daniel is arranged?
ev: Name Daniel and his three friends with their Babylonian names (1:6-7)
Say which kings Daniel served (1:21, 5:31, 6:28)
Describe the two halves of the book: stories (1-6) and visions (7-12)

nodes.d: While Daniel prays, Gabriel comes to give him understanding: seventy weeks are determined for his people and the holy city to finish transgression and bring in everlasting righteousness, with the Messiah the Prince, a city rebuilt, a Messiah cut off, and a desolation.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Gabriel says the seventy weeks are for in Daniel 9:24?
ev: Say when Gabriel comes and why (9:20-23)
List what the seventy weeks are for (9:24)
Report what is said of the Messiah the Prince and of the city and the sanctuary (9:25-27)

nodes.d: Zechariah, prophet in the second year of Darius, receives a call to return, eight night visions about Jerusalem, Joshua and Zerubbabel, answers about fasting and promises for Zion, and two later burdens about the shepherd, the pierced one and the day of the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Zechariah as visions, a question about fasting and two later burdens?
ev: Say that chapters 1-6 are visions and 7-8 answer a question about fasting
Name the two 'burdens' of 9-11 and 12-14 (9:1, 12:1)

nodes.t: A fountain opened; the shepherd smitten
nodes.d: In that day a fountain is opened for sin and uncleanness and idols and false prophets are cut off; the LORD calls the sword against his shepherd, the sheep are scattered, and a third part is refined as silver and calls on his name.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the fountain of Zechariah 13:1 and what the LORD says about the shepherd and the refined third in 13:7-9?
ev: Read 13:1
Say what the LORD calls the sword to do (13:7)
Describe the refining of the third part (13:9)

nodes.d: The burden of the word of the LORD to Israel by Malachi: a series of disputes in which the LORD states a charge, the people ask how, and he answers, ending with the coming day of the LORD and the promise to send Elijah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Malachi's disputes work and how the book ends?
ev: Notice the pattern of 'Wherein?' questions (1:2, 1:6, 2:17, 3:7-8)
Say how the book ends (4:5-6)

nodes.d: The LORD announces a messenger to prepare the way before him and the LORD coming suddenly to his temple, like a refiner's fire who purifies the sons of Levi; he will be a swift witness against sinners, for he does not change.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe who is coming in Malachi 3:1 and what he does in 3:2-3?
ev: Say what is promised in 3:1
Describe the refiner (3:2-3)
Read 3:6

nodes.d: Jesus comes from Galilee to be baptized by John to fulfil all righteousness; the heavens open, the Spirit descends like a dove and a voice calls him beloved Son.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened when Jesus was baptized?
ev: Describe what was seen and heard at the Jordan
Say what Jesus told John in 3:15

nodes.d: After forty days of fasting Jesus is tempted three times by the devil and answers each with “it is written”; the devil leaves and angels minister to him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the devil offered Jesus and how Jesus replied?
ev: List the three temptations
Say what Jesus answered each time

nodes.t: Jesus begins in Galilee and calls fishermen
nodes.d: Hearing John is imprisoned, Jesus moves to Capernaum, preaches repentance for the kingdom of heaven, calls Peter, Andrew, James and John from their nets, and heals great crowds.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jesus called his first disciples?
ev: Name the four fishermen Jesus called
Summarise what Jesus did throughout Galilee (4:23-25)

nodes.t: Healing a leper and the centurion’s servant
nodes.d: Coming down from the mountain, Jesus cleanses a leper by a touch and heals a centurion’s servant with a word, marvelling at the centurion’s faith and saying many will come from east and west to the kingdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the centurion said and how Jesus responded?
ev: Describe the two healings
Say what Jesus said about the centurion’s faith

nodes.t: Healing Peter’s mother-in-law and many others
nodes.d: Jesus heals Peter’s wife’s mother of a fever and, that evening, casts out spirits and heals all who are brought; Matthew links this to a word of Isaiah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Jesus did in Peter’s house and that evening?
ev: Retell the healing in Peter’s house
Say what Matthew says was fulfilled in 8:17

nodes.d: A great tempest swamps the boat while Jesus sleeps; the disciples wake him, he rebukes winds and sea, and they marvel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened on the boat and what the disciples wondered?
ev: Retell the storm in order
Say what the disciples asked in 8:27

nodes.t: The two demon-possessed men and the swine
nodes.d: On the far shore two fierce men from the tombs meet Jesus; the demons ask to enter a herd of swine, which run into the sea, and the city begs Jesus to leave.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the demons asked and how the townspeople responded?
ev: Retell what happened to the swine
Describe the town’s response

nodes.d: Seeing faith, Jesus tells a paralysed man his sins are forgiven; when scribes call it blasphemy, he heals the man to show the Son of man has power on earth to forgive sins.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the healing and what Jesus said about forgiving sins?
ev: Explain why the scribes objected
Say how Jesus showed his authority

nodes.t: Matthew called and eating with sinners
nodes.d: Jesus calls Matthew the tax collector, eats with publicans and sinners, and answers the Pharisees that the sick need a physician and that he came to call sinners.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus ate with publicans and sinners?
ev: Say who Jesus called and where he found him
Explain the “physician” saying

nodes.d: Asked why his disciples do not fast, Jesus speaks of the bridegroom being taken away, and of new cloth on old garments and new wine in old bottles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus’ answer about fasting?
ev: State the question from John’s disciples
Explain one of the two pictures in 9:16-17

nodes.t: The ruler’s daughter and the woman with the issue of blood
nodes.d: On his way to a ruler’s dead daughter, Jesus is touched by a woman with a twelve-year bleeding, whom he calls daughter and heals; then he raises the girl.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jesus helped the woman and the ruler’s daughter?
ev: Retell both healings in order
Say what Jesus told the woman

nodes.t: The twelve named and sent out
nodes.d: Jesus gives the twelve authority to heal and cast out spirits, names them, and sends them to the lost sheep of Israel to preach the kingdom, with instructions about provision and receiving.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell who Jesus sent and what he told them to do?
ev: Name several of the twelve
List the instructions about what to take and what to say

nodes.d: Pharisees object that the disciples pluck grain on the sabbath; Jesus cites David eating the shewbread and the priests in the temple, and says the Son of man is Lord of the sabbath.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus said about David and the sabbath?
ev: Explain the Pharisees’ objection
Say what examples Jesus gave

nodes.t: Healing the withered hand and the chosen servant
nodes.d: In the synagogue Jesus heals a man’s withered hand on the sabbath after saying it is lawful to do good; the Pharisees plot, and Matthew says his gentle ministry fulfils Isaiah’s word of the chosen servant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus healed on the sabbath and what the Pharisees planned?
ev: Retell the healing and the reason Jesus gave
Say what the Pharisees did next

nodes.t: The Beelzebub accusation and the unpardonable word
nodes.d: After a blind and mute man is healed, the Pharisees say Jesus casts out devils by Beelzebub; he answers that a divided kingdom falls, that he casts out by the Spirit of God, and warns of blasphemy against the Holy Ghost and of the words people speak.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the Pharisees claimed and how Jesus answered?
ev: Summarise Jesus’ reply about a divided kingdom
Say what he teaches about the heart and words

nodes.d: When his mother and brothers wait outside, Jesus points to his disciples and says whoever does the will of his Father in heaven is his brother, sister and mother.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who Jesus calls his mother and brothers?
ev: Retell the scene
Say who Jesus names as his family

nodes.d: Jesus tells of seed falling on the path, stony ground, thorns and good ground, explains why he speaks in parables, and interprets the sower for his disciples.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what each soil in the parable stands for?
ev: Retell the four soils
Give the explanation Jesus gave for each

nodes.t: The mustard seed and the leaven
nodes.d: Jesus compares the kingdom of heaven to a tiny mustard seed that becomes a tree and to leaven hidden in three measures of meal, and Matthew says he spoke only in parables to the crowd.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the mustard seed and leaven parables and what they say about the kingdom?
ev: Retell the two parables
Say what Matthew says in 13:34-35

nodes.d: In his home synagogue Jesus is questioned as the carpenter’s son whose family they know; they are offended, and he does few mighty works there because of unbelief.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus was not honoured in his own country?
ev: Say why the people were offended
Explain Jesus’ saying about a prophet’s honour

nodes.t: The death of John the Baptist
nodes.d: Herod, hearing of Jesus, thinks John is risen; Matthew recounts how Herod imprisoned John over Herodias and, because of an oath at his birthday, had him beheaded; John’s disciples bury him and tell Jesus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to John the Baptist?
ev: Retell why John was imprisoned
Describe how Herod came to order the execution

nodes.d: Hearing of John, Jesus withdraws; the crowds follow, he heals them, and with five loaves and two fishes he feeds about five thousand men with twelve baskets left over.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Jesus fed the crowd?
ev: Say how much food there was and how much remained
Describe what Jesus did with the loaves

nodes.t: Jesus walks on the sea and Peter sinks
nodes.d: Jesus comes to the disciples on the sea in the fourth watch; Peter walks toward him, fears the wind and begins to sink, and Jesus saves him, after which they worship him and he heals at Gennesaret.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of Jesus and Peter on the water?
ev: Retell what Peter did and why he sank
Say what the disciples said when the wind ceased

nodes.d: Pharisees accuse the disciples of breaking the tradition of the elders; Jesus charges them with voiding God’s commandment by tradition and says what comes out of the heart, not what goes into the mouth, defiles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said defiles a person?
ev: Give Jesus’ example of tradition overriding a commandment
List what comes out of the heart (15:19)

nodes.d: Near Tyre and Sidon a woman of Canaan begs for her daughter; Jesus is at first silent and speaks of the children’s bread, but she answers about crumbs and he praises her faith and heals the girl.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the woman asked and how Jesus responded?
ev: Retell the conversation
Say what Jesus said about her faith

nodes.d: After healing many at the Galilee mountain, Jesus has compassion on a crowd that has been with him three days and feeds four thousand with seven loaves and a few fishes, with seven baskets left.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell this feeding and say how it differs from the five thousand?
ev: Compare this feeding with the earlier one (14:13-21)
Give the numbers of loaves, fishes and baskets

nodes.t: The demand for a sign and the leaven of the Pharisees
nodes.d: Pharisees and Sadducees seek a sign from heaven and Jesus again points to Jonah; he then warns his disciples against the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees, which they take to mean bread but he says is their doctrine.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees is?
ev: Explain what Jesus meant by leaven
Recall the feedings he reminds them of

nodes.d: Asked who they say he is, Peter answers that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the living God; Jesus calls him blessed, speaks of building his church on this rock, and gives the keys of the kingdom.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell who Peter said Jesus is and how Jesus replied?
ev: State what the people said and what Peter said
Say what Jesus told Peter in 16:17-19

nodes.t: The Son of man must suffer; take up your cross
nodes.d: Jesus begins to tell the disciples he must go to Jerusalem, suffer, be killed and raised the third day; Peter rebukes him and is rebuked, and Jesus calls his followers to deny themselves and take up the cross.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said following him costs?
ev: State what Jesus foretold about himself
Explain the call to deny oneself

nodes.d: On a high mountain Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James and John, Moses and Elias appear, and a voice from the cloud says to hear his beloved Son; coming down he speaks of Elias as already come.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell the transfiguration and what the voice said?
ev: Describe what the three disciples saw and heard
Say what Jesus told them to keep silent

nodes.t: The boy with a demon, a second prediction and the temple tax
nodes.d: Jesus heals a boy the disciples could not heal, saying unbelief is the reason and faith like a mustard seed can move mountains; he again foretells his betrayal and resurrection and arranges payment of the tribute through a coin in a fish.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said about faith like a mustard seed?
ev: Say why the disciples could not cast the spirit out
Retell the coin in the fish

nodes.t: Who is greatest, offences and the lost sheep
nodes.d: Asked who is greatest, Jesus sets a child in their midst and calls for conversion and humility, warns against causing little ones to stumble, and tells of the shepherd seeking one lost sheep.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said makes someone greatest in the kingdom?
ev: Explain what Jesus says about becoming like a child
Retell the lost sheep

nodes.d: Tested by Pharisees, Jesus points back to male and female at the beginning and “one flesh”, says what God joined man must not separate, speaks of Moses’ allowance because of hard hearts, and says not all can receive the saying about eunuchs.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus teaches about marriage and why?
ev: Say what Jesus cites from the beginning
Explain why Moses allowed divorce according to 19:8

nodes.d: People bring children for Jesus to lay hands on and pray; the disciples rebuke them, but Jesus says to let them come, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus said about children coming to him?
ev: Retell what the disciples did and Jesus said
Say whose is the kingdom of heaven

nodes.t: The rich young man and rewards of following
nodes.d: A young man asks what good thing earns eternal life; told to keep the commandments and then to sell all and follow, he goes away sorrowful; Jesus speaks of the camel and needle and promises rewards to those who left all.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus asked the young man to do and why it was hard?
ev: Say why the young man left sorrowful
Explain “with God all things are possible”

nodes.t: Third prediction and the call to serve
nodes.d: Going up to Jerusalem Jesus again foretells his betrayal, mockery, crucifixion and rising; the mother of Zebedee’s sons asks for places for them, and Jesus teaches that the great must serve, for the Son of man came to give his life a ransom for many.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said it means to be great among his followers?
ev: Describe what Jesus foretold
Explain what he says about greatness and the ransom

nodes.d: Leaving Jericho, two blind men cry out “Lord, thou son of David”; the crowd tells them to be quiet, but Jesus stops, touches their eyes and they see and follow him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the blind men asked and what happened?
ev: Retell what the blind men cried and Jesus did
Say what they did after receiving sight

nodes.d: Jesus sends two disciples for an ass and colt, and rides toward Jerusalem while crowds spread garments and branches and cry Hosanna to the son of David; Matthew says this fulfils a word about the King coming meek on an ass.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Jesus came into Jerusalem and what the crowds said?
ev: Describe the entry
Say what the crowds shouted

nodes.d: Jesus drives out the buyers and sellers, overturns tables and seats, says the house of prayer has become a den of thieves, heals the blind and lame, and answers the priests about children’s praise.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus overturned the tables?
ev: Say what Jesus did and quoted
Describe what the children cried and the priests’ reaction

nodes.d: Hungry, Jesus finds only leaves on a fig tree and it withers; he tells the astonished disciples that faith without doubt can even move a mountain and that believing prayer receives.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the fig tree and what Jesus taught?
ev: Retell what happened to the tree
Say what Jesus taught about faith and prayer

nodes.d: Priests and elders ask by what authority Jesus acts; he asks whether John’s baptism was from heaven or men, and when they will not answer he will not answer them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Jesus replied to the question about his authority?
ev: State their question and Jesus’ counter-question
Explain why they would not answer

nodes.t: The parable of the wicked tenants
nodes.d: Tenants of a vineyard beat and kill the owner’s servants and then his son; Jesus cites the rejected stone made head of the corner, says the kingdom will be taken from them, and the priests perceive he speaks of them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who the servants, son and tenants stand for in the parable?
ev: Retell the parable
Say what the priests understood

nodes.d: Pharisees and Herodians ask whether it is lawful to pay tribute to Caesar; Jesus asks for a coin, asks whose image is on it, and says to render to Caesar what is Caesar’s and to God what is God’s.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus’ reply about the coin?
ev: Say why they asked
Explain Jesus’ answer

nodes.d: Sadducees pose a puzzle about a woman married to seven brothers; Jesus says they err not knowing the scriptures or God’s power, that in the resurrection they are as angels, and that God is God of the living.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Jesus’ answer about the resurrection?
ev: Say what the Sadducees denied
Explain how Jesus uses the words about Abraham, Isaac and Jacob

nodes.d: Asked which is the great commandment, Jesus answers love the Lord with all heart, soul and mind, and love your neighbour as yourself, and says all the law and the prophets hang on these two.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say the two great commandments and what they cover?
ev: State the two commandments
Explain “on these two hang all the law and the prophets”

nodes.d: Jesus asks the Pharisees whose son Christ is; they say David’s, and he asks how David in spirit calls him Lord; no one can answer.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the puzzle Jesus raised about David and the Christ?
ev: Retell the question Jesus asked
Say what the Pharisees could not answer

nodes.t: Woes on the scribes and Pharisees
nodes.d: Jesus tells the crowds to do what the scribes and Pharisees say but not what they do, warns against titles and pride, pronounces seven woes for hypocrisy, and laments over Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus criticised in the scribes and Pharisees?
ev: List several hypocrisies Jesus names
Describe the lament over Jerusalem (23:37-39)

nodes.t: The Olivet discourse: signs and persecution
nodes.d: Leaving the temple, Jesus foretells its destruction; on the Mount of Olives he warns of deceivers, wars, famines and persecution, and says the gospel of the kingdom will be preached to all nations before the end.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the warnings Jesus gave in 24:4-14?
ev: State what the disciples asked in 24:3
Name the events Jesus says are not yet the end

nodes.t: The abomination of desolation and the great tribulation
nodes.d: Jesus tells those in Judaea to flee when they see the abomination of desolation spoken of by Daniel, describes great tribulation and warns against false Christs.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus told his disciples to do when they see the abomination of desolation?
ev: Say what Jesus tells those in Judaea to do
Explain the warning about false Christs

nodes.t: The coming of the Son of man
nodes.d: Jesus says after the tribulation the sun will darken and the Son of man will appear in the clouds and send angels to gather the elect; he gives the fig tree parable and says his words will not pass away.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Jesus said will happen when the Son of man comes?
ev: Describe the signs and the coming
Explain the fig tree lesson

nodes.t: Watch, for no one knows the day
nodes.d: Jesus says no one but the Father knows the day, compares the coming to the days of Noah, and tells disciples to watch and be ready, with the picture of the faithful and evil servant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Jesus told his disciples to be ready?
ev: State who knows the day and hour
Contrast the faithful and the evil servant

nodes.t: The plot, the anointing at Bethany and Judas’ bargain
nodes.d: Two days before Passover the rulers plot to kill Jesus; a woman anoints him at Simon the leper’s house and Jesus calls it for his burial; Judas goes to the chief priests for thirty pieces of silver.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the woman did and what Judas agreed to do?
ev: Retell the anointing and the disciples’ objection
Say what Judas did

nodes.t: The Passover and the Lord’s Supper
nodes.d: At the Passover meal Jesus says one of the twelve will betray him; he gives the bread as his body and the cup as his blood of the new testament shed for many for the remission of sins.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus said at the Passover meal about the cup and bread?
ev: Describe what Jesus said over the bread and the cup
Explain “blood of the new testament” in 26:28

nodes.d: Jesus foretells that the disciples will scatter and Peter will deny him; in Gethsemane he prays three times that the cup may pass but not his will, while the disciples sleep.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus prayed in Gethsemane?
ev: Retell what Jesus prayed
Say what happened to the disciples in the garden

nodes.d: Judas arrives with a crowd and betrays Jesus with a kiss; a disciple cuts off an ear, Jesus tells him to put up the sword and says the scriptures must be fulfilled, and the disciples flee.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened in the garden when Jesus was arrested?
ev: Describe the betrayal
Say what Jesus said about the sword

nodes.t: Jesus before Caiaphas and the council
nodes.d: False witnesses speak against Jesus about the temple; asked if he is the Christ the Son of God he answers and speaks of the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power; the high priest cries blasphemy and they condemn him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the council asked Jesus and what they decided?
ev: Say what the false witnesses claimed
Explain the charge of blasphemy

nodes.d: Peter follows to the high priest’s palace and, challenged three times, denies knowing Jesus; the cock crows, he remembers Jesus’ word and weeps bitterly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Peter denied Jesus and what he did afterwards?
ev: Retell the three denials
Say what Peter did when the cock crew

nodes.d: Pilate asks if Jesus is King of the Jews; Jesus answers little; offered the choice, the crowd demands Barabbas and calls for Jesus to be crucified, and Pilate washes his hands.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Pilate’s trial and the choice of Barabbas?
ev: Say who the crowd chose
Describe what Pilate and his wife said about Jesus

nodes.d: Soldiers mock Jesus with a robe and thorns, Simon of Cyrene carries his cross, he is crucified at Golgotha with two thieves under the title King of the Jews, and passers-by taunt him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jesus was mocked and crucified?
ev: Describe the mocking
List the details of the crucifixion

nodes.d: Darkness covers the land, Jesus cries “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” and yields up the ghost; the temple veil tears, the earth quakes, graves open, and the centurion says truly this was the Son of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what happened when Jesus died?
ev: List the signs at his death
Say what the centurion said

nodes.t: The burial and the guard at the tomb
nodes.d: Joseph of Arimathaea buries Jesus in his new rock tomb; the next day the chief priests ask Pilate to make the tomb secure and set a sealed stone and a watch.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell where Jesus was buried and what the priests did about the tomb?
ev: Say who buried Jesus and where
Explain why the priests wanted a guard

nodes.t: The resurrection and the guards’ report
nodes.d: At dawn an angel rolls back the stone and tells the women Jesus is risen and will meet his disciples in Galilee; Jesus meets the women, and the guards are paid to say the disciples stole the body.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened at the tomb on the first day of the week?
ev: Retell what the angel said
Describe what the guards were told to say

nodes.d: On a mountain in Galilee the eleven see the risen Jesus, some doubt, and he says all power is given to him and tells them to make disciples of all nations, baptizing in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Ghost, with his presence always.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Jesus told his disciples to do and what he promised?
ev: Say what Jesus commanded in 28:19-20
Say what he promises
